title: Finite affine images cover a quasi-compact algebraic space
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], X an algebraic space over S [def-trf-algebraic-space], and assume there exists a quasi-compact scheme atlas Q -> X [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. For every representable surjective etale scheme atlas w:W -> X, there exist n >= 0 and affine opens V_i of W [def-weil-open-immersion], indexed by Fin n, whose composites to X are jointly surjective in the field-extension sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family]. They may be chosen with n=0 if W is empty. No coproduct is asserted and W need not be quasi-compact or separated.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale map $q:Q\to X$ with $Q$ a quasi-compact scheme, as supplied by the hypothesis and the scheme-test definition in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use the point topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology]. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $|q|$ is continuous and surjective. Its image is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact], and its image is all of $|X|$. Thus $|X|$ is quasi-compact. This uses no quasi-compactness of the specified atlas $W$.

source.place: Tag 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space), continuous-surjection direction; Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover), start of converse.

proof.text: Let $(V_a)_{a\in A}$ be the affine open cover of $W$ given by its scheme structure [def-pc-scheme]. For every scheme $T\to X$, representability of $w$ gives the etale scheme $W_T=W\times_XT\to T$. The pullback $V_a\times_WW_T\to W_T$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. It is etale and its composite with $W_T\to T$ is etale by clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The fibre-product universal property identifies this scheme with $V_a\times_XT$. Hence $V_a\to X$ is representable etale by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its image on points is open by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. These images cover $|X|$: a point lifts to $W$ because $w$ is surjective, and the lifted point belongs to some $V_a$. Quasi-compactness from Step 1 now selects finitely many images covering $|X|$. Enumerate the selected affine opens as $W_1,\ldots,W_n$. This is joint surjectivity in [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family]. To verify the displayed field-extension formulation, fix a representative (K,s,x). Its class lies in one selected image. Equality with a representative in that open can be realized over a common extension L of K and its source field: the common-field relation is reflexive and symmetric, and transitivity follows by taking a common overfield of the two extensions over their shared intermediate field. Restrict the source section to L. The map K -> L and this restricted section give exactly the equality in IsJointlySurjective. Thus the finite topological subcover yields the stronger-looking representative formula, with no choice of representatives in a definition.

proof.text: If W is empty, its surjectivity forces X to have no field-valued point classes. Choose n=0 and the empty function of opens. Joint surjectivity is vacuous: a field-valued point of X would lift through W after a field extension, impossible. In the nonempty case use the finite subcover just constructed. This gives the implication IsEmpty W -> n=0 as well as the required field-extension covering condition.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_affine_image_selection {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hqc : ∃ (Q : Over S) (q : yoneda.obj Q ⟶ X.obj.obj), CompactSpace Q.left ∧ IsEtale q ∧ IsSurjective q) (W : Over S) (w : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.obj.obj) (hw : IsEtale w) (hs : IsSurjective w) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (V : Fin n → W.left.Opens), (∀ i : Fin n, IsAffineOpen (V i)) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun i : Fin n ↦ yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk ((V i).ι ≫ W.hom)) (V := W) (V i).ι rfl) ≫ w) ∧ (IsEmpty W.left → n = 0)
